accepted.evidence: DEDR2023 gives Tamil kai, Malayalam kayyi and Kannada kayi hand/arm. Pattapu kayi (source IPA kaji) matches the velar-plus-glide hand stem and combined arm/hand sense; j is the source phonetic glide, rendered y in the existing Jambu form. The proposal uses the full DEDR article; inheritance versus local transmission remains subject to review. Upstream cognacy/alignment labels are discovery aids, not independent evidence.

DEDR3650 explicitly gives Tamil nāy/nāi and Malayalam nāy dog. Pattapu nāi preserves the full simple dog stem. The explicitly analysed -kuṛi element of other languages in this article is absent here and is not supplied. The proposal uses the full DEDR article; inheritance versus local transmission remains subject to review. Upstream cognacy/alignment labels are discovery aids, not independent evidence.

DEDR2674(a) gives Tamil/Malayalam/Kannada/Telugu uppu salt. Pattapu upu has the corresponding salt stem, with the source single-stop transcription preserved. DEDR4085 gives Telugu pāmu and Tamil/Malayalam pāmpu snake, with Kodagu pāmbï. Pattapu pāmu preserves a cluster-reduced form. DEDR3986(a) gives Tamil pal, Malayalam pallu and Telugu palu/pallu tooth. Pattapu polu is a proposed rounded-vowel member of this p-l family. DEDR4707: Tamil/Malayalam mayir denote hair, with Irula moyiru/megaru and Kota/Toda mīr in the same article. DEDR497: Kannada ela/ele and Malayalam ila denote leaf, alongside Tamil ilai. DEDR4410: Tamil/Malayalam pēr and Telugu pēru denote name. Pattapu pēɹu matches the long-vowel rhotic stem; the source’s rhotic transcription is preserved. Whole-article family membership is proposed; inheritance versus local transmission remains subject to review.

DEDR4753: Tamil/Malayalam maḻai/maḻa and Kodagu/Tulu maḷe denote rain. DEDR1298: Kannada kalu/kallu, Telugu kallu and Gondi (Ma.) kalu denote stone, alongside Tamil kal. Pattapu kalu has a direct segmental and semantic comparison within this article. Whole-article family membership is proposed; inheritance versus local transmission remains subject to review.

DEDR4939: Malayalam muṭṭa/moṭṭa, Tamil muṭṭai and Kodagu muṭṭe denote egg. DEDR3559: Telugu tōlu and Kannada tōl(u) explicitly include leather as well as skin/hide, alongside Tamil tōl. Pattapu θōlu retains the long-vowel lateral stem with final u and an initial dental fricative; this is the attested material sense, not an inferred change from bark. Whole-article family membership is proposed; inheritance versus local transmission remains subject to review.

DEDR4240: Telugu poga denotes smoke, alongside Malayalam puka and Kannada/Kodagu poge. Pattapu poga matches the noun directly; tobacco and verbal derivatives in the article are not substituted for its source meaning. Whole-article family membership is proposed; inheritance versus local transmission remains subject to review.

DEDR4559: Tulu poḷtu denotes time, daylight and sun; Kannada portu and Telugu poddu/proddu likewise include sun. Pattapu pold̪u preserves a lateral-plus-dental cluster with a short vowel. Its plain l is not normalized to ḷ and the sun sense is explicit within this whole article. Whole-article family membership is proposed; inheritance versus local transmission remains subject to review.

DEDR3538: Malayalam tōka, Kannada tōke and Telugu tō̃ka denote tail, alongside Tamil tōkai. DEDR1481: Tamil/Malayalam kāṟṟu, Kota ka·ṯ and Kodagu ka·tï denote wind. Pattapu kāθu preserves the long-vowel k-initial stem with a dental fricative corresponding to the dental/alveolar stop series. DEDR2146: Tamil koḻuppu denotes fat and grease; Malayalam koḻuppu denotes fatness and solidity of broth or curry. Pattapu kolupu preserves this suffixed noun with plain l and single p in the source; it is compared with the attested noun rather than assigned an invented synchronic derivation. Whole-article family membership is proposed; inheritance versus local transmission remains subject to review.

DEDR1693: Telugu guṇḍe-kāya, Tulu guṇḍe-kāyi and Kannada guṇḍi-kāyi explicitly denote the physical heart. Pattapu guⁿdekāi matches this full formation. Ordered components are DEDR1693 heart/chest plus DEDR1459 kāy/kāya/kāyi fruit/nut; the latter also includes Kodagu kāy kidneys. Source nasal notation and final diphthong are retained. These are component links, not two alternative whole-word etymologies. Whole-article family membership is proposed; inheritance versus local transmission remains subject to review.

DEDR3684: Tamil/Malayalam nī and Kodagu nī/nīnï are second-person singular pronouns. Pattapu niyi is proposed as the corresponding stem with a glide and final vowel; its short vowels are retained. The two source records specify female and male addressees but have identical forms, so both records remain distinct without inventing a morphological gender contrast. Whole-article family membership is proposed; inheritance versus local transmission remains subject to review.

DEDR1: Kodagu ava explicitly means that woman, alongside Tamil/Malayalam avaḷ. DEDR1: Tamil/Malayalam avan and Kodagu avëⁿ mean that man. Pattapu avã retains the av- stem with a nasalized final vowel instead of a separately written final nasal. DEDR5297: Tamil/Malayalam vaḻi and Kannada baḻi denote way, path or road. Pattapu voli is proposed with a rounded first vowel and plain lateral retained. DEDR1941: Malayalam ceṭi denotes shrub or small tree, Kannada ceṭṭu includes tree in general, and Telugu ceṭṭu denotes tree, plant, bush or creeper. DEDR3610: Tamil/Malayalam nallatu means that which is good, Kodagu nallë means good, and Gondi (M.) nelā has an e-vowel. DEDR4275: Tamil/Malayalam putu and Kota pud denote new; Kannada/Tulu posa show another medial consonant outcome in this family. DEDR3758: Irula nä·ṯṯu denotes yesterday and Kota nē·r has the oblique stem nē·ṯ-. Pattapu nēt̪u matches the long front vowel and dental-stop formation particularly closely. DEDR844: Tamil ellām and Malayalam ellām/ellāvum denote all, alongside Kannada/Telugu ella. Pattapu alāmu preserves the lateral-long-vowel-m formation with an initial a, a single lateral and final u. DEDR2041: Telugu koncemu explicitly means a little or a few, and Kannada koñce a little; Tamil/Malayalam koñcam gives the related quantity noun. DEDR1931: Tamil cēppu is listed among redness forms and Malayalam cōppu means red/red colour. DEDR4680 gives Telugu maṇṭa flame, blaze and Tamil maṇṭu to blaze up or glow. Pattapu maⁿta preserves the nasal-stop formation with its non-retroflex t and the broader source meaning fire retained. Inheritance versus local transmission remains subject to review; the Telugu comparison alone does not establish borrowing.

DEDR5276 explicitly gives Telugu baluvu heavy, great, strong and Kannada bolu strength, firmness, bigness. DEDR1851: Telugu kuṟuca explicitly means short, dwarfish, small, and Kannada kuṟucu/kuṟaci denotes smallness or dwarfishness. DEDR5151: Irula dāru explicitly means who; Kannada dāru and Kodagu dā·rï occur in the same interrogative article. Pattapu d̪āɹu closely matches the initial dental, long vowel and rhotic formation. This specific d-initial member supports the whole-article link even though Tamil yā/e- forms dominate the head. Whole-article family membership is proposed; inheritance versus local transmission remains subject to review.

DEDR3939: Tamil paiyaṉ/paiyal denote boy, while Tulu paiyya denotes child and paiyyè child or boy. Pattapu paii is proposed as a contracted member of this family, with its written vowel sequence retained. The absence of an overt glide or final consonant is an explicit limitation; no spelling correction or exact-form claim is made. Whole-article family membership is proposed; inheritance versus local transmission remains subject to review.

DEDR1594: Tamil ciṟukki and Malayalam ceṟukki explicitly denote girl; Pattapu siɹiki preserves the sibilant-rhotic-k formation with raised vowels and an ungeminated k. Whole-article family membership is proposed; inheritance versus local transmission remains subject to review.

DEDR4666(b) explicitly gives Konda maṇu, Parji man and Kodagu maṇa sand, alongside Tamil/Malayalam maṇal. DEDR3045 explicitly records Tamil taṇṇīr/taṇṇi cold water, water and Malayalam taṇṇīr/taṇṇi cold/drinking water, beside taṇ cold; DEDR3690 gives nīr water. Proposed ordered historical components are cold3045 plus water3690. Pattapu θani compares with the attested shortened taṇṇi form, retaining θ and its single non-retroflex n. The lexicalized water meaning is preserved; the proposal does not assert that this is synchronically transparent in Pattapu or establish an immediate donor route.

DEDR399 includes Kodagu āṇï man/male and Tulu āṇů male, alongside Kannada āṇma/āṇba husband and Tamil āḷ husband. Pattapu ānɛ is proposed in this whole male/person family with its plain n and final ɛ retained. The husband sense is supported within the article, but this is not an exact same-form-and-sense attestation; local sound history and inheritance versus transmission remain subject to review.

Proposed ordered components: front795 plus chest/breast4818. DEDR795 gives Telugu/Tulu eduru front/forepart;4818 gives Malayalam māṟu chest and Tamil mār breast/chest. These account for both portions of Pattapu ed̪uɹumāɹu with its dental and rhotic notation preserved. The separate simple breast mola record remains distinct.

held.reason: Full DEDR156 gives Kannada apa/appa and Tamil appaṉ father. Pattapu yāpa has initial y and a long vowel absent from these basic forms. Compare the parallel yāma mother and yaka older sister before deciding whether the initial material belongs to the stem or a possessive formation; nursery-word resemblance alone does not establish inheritance or an immediate donor.

Full DEDR183 gives Kannada/Telugu ama/amma and Tamil ammā mother, but does not explain Pattapu initial yā-. Its parallelism with yāpa father requires a local morphological or phonological account. No component or direct reflex is assigned merely from the familiar nursery stem.

Full DEDR23 gives Telugu/Kannada akka and Kodagu akkë elder sister. Tamil’s initial subsection has different elder-female kin roles; the Telugu discovery supplies the exact elder-sister sense. Pattapu initial y remains unexplained, especially beside yāpa/yāma; investigate possession or prothesis before assigning the whole response.

Full DEDR2453 gives Tamil cāmpal/cāmpar and Malayalam cāmpal ashes. Pattapu sāmulu has a matching long vowel but lacks the p of these forms and differs in the remaining vowels. Investigate an attested local variant or another family before assigning; source spelling and ash meaning remain unchanged.

Full DEDR2623 gives Telugu cīma and Kolami sīma ant, but does not explain Pattapu medial tɹ or short vowel. DEDR1548 cital/cedalu is specifically termite/white ant and does not directly explain the final m. Neither is assigned from the ant gloss alone; preserve sitɹam and investigate a primary Pattapu or closely related dialect source.

Full DEDR1235 gives Telugu kampa/krampa thorny branch or bramble, Gadaba kampa thorny bushes for fencing and questioned Kannada kompe bundle of thorny twigs. The article does not directly attest general firewood, and Pattapu final ⁿge remains unexplained. Need local morphology and semantic evidence before assigning the whole form; do not split the ending into an invented component.

Full DEDR3999 has Tamil paḻacu/paḻaiya old, Kodagu paḷe/paḷēdï and related forms; Pattapu palçi has a plausible initial stem but its final çi and contraction are not explained by the quoted forms. Check local inflection or a primary dialectal form before assigning the whole response.

Full DEDR3939 supports the pay-/paiy- child/boy family, including Tamil paiyaṉ, Tulu paiyya and Malayalam paśuṅṅaḷ children. Pattapu payaŋgu has an unexplained final ŋgu and source gloss child; investigate local number morphology before treating the complete response as a simple reflex. The Malayalam plural comparison is not itself proof of Pattapu plurality.

Percival1862 p225 unproofread transcription attests Telugu tala/talakaya head; a third-party Brown p515 transcription describes kāya as a colloquial affix. Full DEDR3103/1459 support the stems but relation type (compound versus affixal extension) and primary scan verification remain unresolved. See head-compound-research.md for exact URLs and retrieval limitations. No direct borrowing route is established.
